newsitem.title: USA: CME hog futures end higher but off fresh highs.
newsitem.headline: CME hog futures end higher but off fresh highs.

text.p: CME hog futures posted new contract highs in June through August and distant June and July before retreating somewhat late on profit taking to close with pared gains, traders said. Pork bellies followed and ended mostly lower on local selling, traders said.

Hogs closed 0.075 to 0.550 cent per lb higher with June up 0.375 at 83.075 cents. June set a contract high earlier at 83.400 cents with July notching a fresh high at 83.000 cents and August at 80.375 cents.
Pork bellies finished mostly 0.100 cent per lb higher to 0.350 lower with only August up and May off 82.600 cents. November fresh closed up 2.000 at 51.000 cents.
Stronger cash hog ideas for Wednesday and persistent strength from Taiwan's pork ban prompted early buying. But profit taking developed after futures set highs, traders said.

Declines were curbed, however, by expectations hog runs may tighten soon on a seasonal basis. Demand for pork is also seen up in the next couple of months as previous customers of Taiwan, especially Japan, begin replenishing stocks.
"That's underlying everthing," said Karl Skold, director of research for Frontier Risk Management of the Taiwan pork export ban's influence on CME hog futures.
The Dutch pork ban is also a bullish factor, traders said.
Technicians also cited bullish chart configurations. Weekly charts point to a much higher price level in hog futures, especially after April contract went off the board, they said.

LIT division of First Options bought June late while locals, Lind-Waldock and Rand Financials were late sellers. In hog options, Rosenthal Collins bought August 78 to 86 calls while locals bought June out of the money 72 to 74 puts early. RBH spread long June 83 puts/short 81 puts on a one for two basis late. Volatility was soft early, pit sources said.

Pork belly futures traded on both sides of previous levels following hog futures and fell late on profit taking. Local selling pushed values down for net losses but scattered support ahead of an expected bullish CME Out-of-Town report kept the market supported, traders said.
Refco and ABN Chicogo Corp were cited as buyers against the local pressure, pit sources said.
After the close the CME reported the weekly out-of-town storage movement at a net in of 353,000 lbs. This compared with estimates of unchanged to in 350,000 lbs.
